name: Cap daily AI spend per workflow and alert in Slack

parameters.content:
## Cap daily AI spend per workflow and alert in Slack

n8n counts executions, not dollars. A looping agent, an unexpectedly busy day
or a prompt that pulls in far more context than you planned can run up a large
model bill overnight, and nothing in the platform stops it or tells you. This
is a sub-workflow that gives every AI workflow its own daily ceiling.

### How it works

An AI workflow calls this twice. Before the model, with action check, it gets
back whether the call fits inside today's remaining budget, so a runaway is
stopped at the next call rather than found on the invoice. After the model,
with action record, it passes the usage object straight through and the call
is priced and added to the day's total. Prices sit in a sheet rather than in
the code, because they change every few weeks, and a model missing from that
sheet is charged at a deliberately pessimistic fallback rate rather than
counted as free, which is how budgets quietly stop working. Each workflow gets
its own cap and its own Slack channel from a Budgets tab, with one row named
default catching everything else. The day boundary follows the offset you set,
not UTC midnight. Slack is told once when the warning line is crossed and once
when the cap is reached, never on every call after. The next morning, one
message reports what each workflow cost and which ones ran into their ceiling.

### Setup

Connect Sheets and Slack, create the data table with the columns on the ledger
node, and fill the Budgets and Model Prices tabs.

### Note

This caps workflows that call it. It cannot police one that does not, so wire
it into the expensive ones first.

## Read the request, find the budget
One entry point for both jobs. The caller is matched to a budget row, with a default row catching the rest, and the day boundary follows your offset rather than UTC midnight.

## Answer before the money is spent
The pre-flight check. The caller branches on allowed and skips the model call when today's ceiling would be passed, so a loop is stopped at the next call.

## Price what was spent, warn once
Tokens are priced from the sheet, an unpriced model is charged at the fallback rate rather than treated as free, and Slack hears about the crossing once rather than on every call after it.

## The morning after
One message says what each workflow cost yesterday and which ones ran into their ceiling. Nothing is posted on a quiet day.

nodes.name: Called By Your AI Workflow
nodes.notes: Call this twice from an AI workflow. Before the model: action=check, workflow, estimatedUsd or estimatedTokens. After it: action=record, workflow, model, and the usage object from the model node.

nodes.name: Load Budgets
nodes.notes: Budgets tab columns: Workflow, Daily Cap USD, Warn At Percent, Slack Channel, UTC Offset, Unknown Model USD Per Million. Keep one row named default as the catch-all.

nodes.name: Load Model Prices
nodes.notes: Model Prices tab columns: Model, Input USD Per Million, Output USD Per Million. Prices live here rather than in code because they change every few weeks.

nodes.name: Read Today's Ledger Row
nodes.notes: Data table columns: dayKey (string), date (string), workflow (string), usd (number), calls (number), warned (string), blocked (string)

nodes.name: Return The Decision
nodes.notes: Branch on allowed in the calling workflow. False means skip the model call and take whatever fallback you have.

nodes.name: Crossed A Threshold?
nodes.notes: Only the crossing is announced. Without this check every call after eighty percent would post to Slack again.
